draft.title: Who the revolution left out
card: Loyalists
Loyalists stayed loyal to Britain. Many lost homes and land, and tens of thousands left the new United States for Britain, Canada or elsewhere.
Enslaved people
Slavery continued in much of the new nation. Some northern states began to end it, but most enslaved people stayed in bondage, mainly in the South.
Women
Women were praised for supporting the cause, but they gained few new legal or political rights. Most could not vote, and married women had little legal control over property.
Native Americans
Native nations gained little. Many had sided with Britain, and the new nation's growth westward put pressure on their lands.
draft.remember: The revolution brought liberty to many white men, but loyalists lost out and others gained little.

a.q: What happened to most enslaved people in the new United States after the revolution?
opts: They stayed enslaved, mainly in the South
They were freed across the whole nation
They gained the vote in the northern states
They were sent to Canada with the loyalists
a.why: Slavery continued in much of the new nation, and most enslaved people stayed in bondage. Some northern states began to end slavery, but that did not free people across the whole nation.
a.clue: Only some northern states began to act.

b.q: Hannah lived in Massachusetts in 1785. She had supported the patriot cause and ran her late husband's farm. Which statement best describes how the revolution affected women like her?
opts: She was honoured for her support but gained few new rights
She gained full political rights through her wartime support
She lost her land because she backed the patriot cause
She was treated as a loyalist because she was a woman
b.why: Women were praised for backing the cause but gained few new legal or political rights. Her support did not lead to the vote, so the option claiming full political rights is wrong, even though her role was valued.
b.clue: Praise and new rights are not the same thing.

a.best: They stayed enslaved, mainly in the South

b.best: She was honoured for her support but gained few new rights

problems.detail: The remember line says the revolution 'brought liberty to many white men', but the card never teaches this. Students are asked to remember a claim the card does not support.

Hannah is a widow running her late husband's farm. Widows had more legal control over property than the married women the card describes, so the scenario sits awkwardly with the card's property point. The intended answer still holds.

check.summary: The facts and both answers are sound. Two minor issues: the remember line adds a claim about liberty for white men that the card does not teach, and the widow in question b does not quite match the card's point about married women's property.
